The 300-sample SuperCon slice is dominated by a clear structure–Tc pattern: **layered cuprates** sit far above everything else. After parsing each formula into atomic fractions, the useful signals are:

| Family | Example | Tc (K) | Design-element fractions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hg-1223 | HgBa₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈ | **132** | O=0.5, Cu=0.1875, Ba=0.125, Ca=0.125 |
| 1223-like (O undercounted) | Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O | 126 | O=0.125, Cu=0.375, Ba=0.25, Ca=0.25 |
| Tl/Pb-1223 | Tl₀.₅Pb₀.₅Ba₁.₆Sr₀.₄Ca₂Cu₃O | 120 | O≈0.11, Cu≈0.33, Ba≈0.18, Ca≈0.22, Pb≈0.056 |
| Bi-2223 / Bi-2212 | Bi₂Sr₂Ca₁Cu₂O₁₀ | 110 | O, Cu, Sr, Ca, Bi |
| YBCO | YBa₂Cu₃O₇ | ~93 | O≈0.54, Cu≈0.23, Ba≈0.15, Y≈0.077 |
| H₂S | H₂S | 185 | **none** of the 20 elements |

Tree surrogates trained on the 20 design fractions agree with that ranking (ensemble ~120 K on the Hg-1223 vector vs ~119 K on Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O vs ~84 K on YBCO). H₂S cannot be targeted: its design vector is the zero vector, which is shared with many ~0–10 K metals, and the model predicts ~8 K.

The single best supported point is therefore the Hg-1223 design vector (highest labeled Tc that uses these elements, complete oxygen count, best surrogate score). Implicit Hg (fraction 0.0625) is outside the design set; leaving that remainder unspecified is exactly how that row appears in the 20-D feature space. Unused variables stay at the lower bound.

print("Tc range:", df['target'].min(), df['target'].max())

    """Parse compact formula into element counts"""
    pattern = r'([A-Z][a-z]?)(\d*\.?\d*)'
    matches = re.findall(pattern, formula)
    counts = {}
    for el, num in matches:
        n = float(num) if num else 1.0
        counts[el] = counts.get(el, 0) + n
    return counts

def to_fractions(counts):
    total = sum(counts.values())
    if total == 0:
        return {}
    return {el: c/total for el, c in counts.items()}

    for el in elements:
